page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the configuration delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with support for VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration featuring AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Hardware resource distribution excludes local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote block storage solutions. The server does not bundle dedicated graphics processing units, and networking is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool.

Empirical benchmark testing indicates strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 3072.98 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2000.0, placing both within the top 25 percent tier. Multi-core performance profiles align with middle-tier expectations, recording 24601.13 in stress-ng multi-core and 11705.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth demonstrated lower throughput at 36.9 GB/sec, representing a bottom-quartile result, whereas cached small-block memory reads achieved 1216.18 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 21.68 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 17.55 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a cost-efficient resource profile for processing-dense environments where excessive RAM allocation is unnecessary. Potential tradeoffs stem from the absence of integrated local storage and lower large-block memory read bandwidth. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is suited for continuous integration and compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch data transformations, and CPU-bound application tier microservices.
